newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Striking Brazilian police battle army.
newsitem.headline: Striking Brazilian police battle army.

text.p: At least three people were injured when striking Brazilian police officers battled with army units in the trouble-ridden northeastern state of Alagoas on Thursday, officials said.

Officials said the clash, in which up to 400 rounds were fired, occurred after the head of the legislative assembly in the state capital Maceio requested military protection against demonstrating police, on strike over unpaid wages.

"The president of the assembly asked the military to protect the legislative building and that's when the fighting happened," said Romani Roland, head of the Maceio branch of the National Order of Lawyers.
Roland said at least three police officers were injured but commanders of the 250 soldiers denied they were responsible.
"My troops were shot at, we don't know where from, but we did not shoot back. We fired into the air," Colonel Antonio Carlos told national CBN radio.
The colonel said it was possible the three injured police officers had been shot by their colleagues, adding: "In confusion like that it's difficult to know where you're shooting."

Alagoas has sunk into chaos over the past two years because of severe financial problems. The state assembly had been due to vote on Thursday on the impeachment of governor Divaldo Suruagy, allegedly involved in the fraudulent issue of state bonds.
A spokeswoman said Suruagy requested a six-month leave of absence on Thursday.

In the federal capital Brasilia, Justice Minister Iris Resende was expected to head to Maceio later on Thursday and the government was expected to decide whether or not to intervene in the state. Brasilia has already taken over the financial management of Alagoas.
